title: Christstollen (German Christmas fruit bread with marzipan)

ingredients.name: soft butter, plus 100 g melted for brushing

steps: Soak the raisins and candied peel in the rum for at least an hour, ideally overnight.
Stir the yeast and a spoonful of the sugar into the warm milk and leave for 10 minutes until foamy.
Mix the flour, remaining sugar, spices, lemon zest, soft butter, egg and the yeast milk, and knead into a smooth dough. Cover and let rise for 1 hour.
Knead in the soaked fruit, any remaining rum and the almonds, then let the dough rest for 20 minutes.
Roll the dough into an oval about 25 by 30 cm. Shape the marzipan into a log and lay it along the centre, then fold one long side over and press lightly to make the classic stollen shape.
Place on a lined tray, let rise for 30 minutes, then bake at 180 C for 50 to 60 minutes until deep golden.
Brush generously with melted butter while hot, dust thickly with icing sugar, then cool, wrap well and rest for several days before slicing.

title: Currywurst (Berlin sausage with spiced curry-ketchup sauce)

ingredients.name: pork bratwurst or similar fresh sausages
chips or bread rolls, to serve

steps: Soften the onion in the oil over medium heat for about 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and half the curry powder and paprika and cook for a minute until fragrant.
Add the ketchup, water, sugar and Worcestershire sauce and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes until thick and glossy, then season and blend smooth if you prefer.
Pan-fry or grill the sausages for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through.
Slice the sausages into thick rounds, pour the hot sauce over them and dust with the remaining curry powder.
Serve immediately with chips or a bread roll.

title: Gaisburger Marsch (Swabian beef stew with potatoes and spaetzle)

ingredients.name: beef brisket or shin on the bone
fresh spaetzle (store-bought, or 250 g flour, 2 eggs and about 100 ml water)
onions, sliced and fried in butter until golden

steps: Put the beef in a large pot with 2 litres of cold water, bring slowly to a boil and skim off the foam.
Add the halved onion, one carrot, half the leek, the celeriac, bay leaves and salt, then simmer gently for about 2 hours until the meat is tender.
Lift out the meat and cut it into bite-size pieces. Strain the broth and discard the soft vegetables.
Dice the second carrot and the remaining leek, and cook them with the potatoes in the strained broth for 15 minutes until tender.

If making your own spaetzle, beat the flour, eggs, water and salt into a thick elastic batter, then press it through a spaetzle press or scrape it from a board into simmering salted water. Cook until they float, then lift them out.
Add the meat and spaetzle to the pot to heat through and adjust the seasoning.
Ladle into deep bowls and top with the golden fried onions and chives.

title: Käsespätzle (Swabian and Allgäu cheese noodles with fried onions)
steps: Beat the flour, eggs, water, salt and nutmeg into a thick, elastic batter that falls slowly from a spoon, and let it rest for 15 minutes.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Press the batter through a spaetzle press or scrape thin strips from a wet board into the water.
Cook in batches until the spaetzle float, then lift them out with a slotted spoon.
Fry the sliced onions in half of the butter over medium heat for 15 to 20 minutes until deep golden and sweet.
In a warm ovenproof dish, layer the spaetzle with the grated cheese and keep the layers warm in a low oven until the cheese melts. Stir the layers through once.
Top with the fried onions, the remaining butter and the chives, and serve straight from the dish, with a green salad.

title: Königsberger Klopse (poached meatballs in creamy caper sauce)

ingredients.name: minced meat, half beef and half pork
stale bread roll, soaked in milk and squeezed out
salt, pepper and nutmeg to taste

steps: Mix the minced meat with the squeezed bread, onion, anchovies, egg, salt, pepper and a little nutmeg until the mixture is evenly combined and slightly sticky.
Bring the stock to a gentle simmer with the bay leaves. Shape the meat mixture into 8 to 12 balls with wet hands.
Lower the meatballs into the stock and poach them gently, never at a hard boil, for about 15 to 20 minutes until they float and are cooked through.
Lift out the meatballs and keep them warm, then strain the stock and measure out about 500 ml.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in the flour and cook for a minute without browning, then whisk in the hot stock gradually and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir the egg yolk into the cream, add a spoonful of hot sauce to it, then whisk it back into the pan off the heat. Add the capers and lemon juice and season.
Return the meatballs to the sauce to heat through and serve with boiled potatoes or rice.

title: Maultaschen (Swabian filled pasta pockets with spinach and meat in broth)

ingredients.name: minced pork or mixed pork and beef
spinach, blanched, squeezed dry and chopped
stale bread roll, soaked in milk and squeezed
onion, finely chopped and softened in butter
salt, pepper and nutmeg to taste
onions, sliced and fried in butter, to serve

steps: Knead the flour, 3 eggs, oil, a pinch of salt and a little water into a smooth, firm dough. Wrap and rest it for 30 minutes.
For the filling, mix the minced meat, spinach, soaked bread, softened onion, parsley and the filling egg. Season well with salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Roll the dough out thinly into long sheets, about 12 cm wide, and spread the filling in a thin even layer over one half of each sheet.
Fold the empty half over the filling, press down, and mark and cut the strip into rectangles about 8 cm long. Press the edges to seal.
Bring the broth to a gentle simmer and cook the Maultaschen for about 15 minutes until they float and are cooked through.
Serve the pockets in the hot broth sprinkled with chives, or slice and pan-fry them in butter with scrambled egg, topped with fried onions.

title: Reibekuchen (Rhenish crisp potato pancakes with apple sauce)
steps: Grate the potatoes and onion on the coarse side of a box grater into a bowl.
Tip the mixture into a clean tea towel and squeeze out as much liquid as you can. Let the drained liquid stand for a minute and pour off the water, keeping the starch that settles at the bottom.
Return the potato to the bowl and mix in the starch, eggs, flour, salt and pepper.
Heat about 1 cm of oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.
Spoon in portions of the batter, flatten them to thin discs and fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp at the edges.
Drain on paper towels and keep warm in a low oven while you fry the rest. Serve hot with apple sauce, or with smoked salmon or dark bread and butter.

title: Sauerbraten (Rhenish pot roast marinated in vinegar and spices)

ingredients.name: beef roast such as topside or bottom round
gingersnap biscuits, crumbled (or 1 tbsp sugar plus 1 tbsp flour)

steps: Bring the vinegar, water, onions, carrot, celery, bay leaves, cloves, juniper and peppercorns to a boil, then let the marinade cool completely.
Place the beef in a deep non-metal bowl, pour the cold marinade over it so the meat is mostly covered, and refrigerate for 2 to 3 days, turning the meat once a day.
Lift the meat out, pat it very dry and strain the marinade, keeping both the liquid and the vegetables.
Season the beef with salt and pepper and brown it on all sides in hot lard in a heavy casserole, then take it out and brown the marinade vegetables in the same pot.
Return the meat, add about 500 ml of the strained marinade and the raisins, cover and simmer very gently, or cook in a 160 C oven, for about 2 to 2.5 hours until tender.

Remove the meat and keep it warm. Strain the sauce, bring it to a simmer and stir in the crumbled gingersnaps until it thickens and turns slightly sweet and tangy. Adjust with salt, pepper and a pinch of sugar or splash of marinade.
Slice the roast against the grain and serve with the sauce, potato dumplings or boiled potatoes and red cabbage.

title: Schweinshaxe (Bavarian roast pork knuckle with crackling)

ingredients.name: raw pork hocks (knuckles), about 1 kg each
cornflour mixed with water, to thicken (optional)

steps: Score the skin of each hock in a diamond pattern with a sharp knife, cutting through the skin but not into the meat.
Rub the hocks all over with salt, crushed garlic and ground caraway, working the seasoning into the cuts.
Heat the oven to 160 C. Scatter the onion, carrot, celery and bay leaves in a roasting tin, set the hocks on top and pour in the stock.
Roast for about 1.5 hours, basting with a little beer every 20 minutes or so, until the meat starts to pull away from the bone.
Raise the oven to 220 C, brush the skin with more beer and roast for 30 to 40 minutes until the crackling is blistered and crisp.
Rest the hocks for 10 minutes. Strain the roasting juices, simmer them for a few minutes and thicken lightly with the cornflour if you like.
Serve with potato dumplings or boiled potatoes, sauerkraut and the gravy.

title: Zwiebelkuchen (German onion tart with bacon and caraway)

ingredients.name: salt, pepper and nutmeg to taste

steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the warm milk and melted butter and knead into a smooth dough. Cover and leave in a warm place for about 1 hour until doubled.
Fry the bacon in a large pan until the fat runs, add the onions and cook gently for 15 to 20 minutes until soft and translucent but not brown. Let them cool.
Whisk the sour cream with the eggs, caraway, salt, pepper and a little nutmeg, then fold in the onions and bacon.
Heat the oven to 200 C. Roll the dough out to fit a greased baking tray or 28 cm tart tin, pushing a slight rim up the edge.
Spread the onion filling over the dough and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the custard is set and the top is golden.
Serve warm in squares, traditionally with new wine or cider in autumn.
